subject: CAR
body: A personal development plan (PDP) helps you
options: identify learning needs and plan training
explanation: Review it regularly with your manager.

subject: CAR
body: Reflective practice means
options: thinking about your work to learn and improve
explanation: Feedback from others helps you reflect.

subject: CAR
body: If you have a dilemma between a person's rights and their safety, you should
options: seek advice from your manager and record your actions
explanation: Balance their rights with the duty to keep them safe.

subject: CAR
body: Complaints from people who use services should be
options: taken seriously and handled through the complaints procedure
explanation: Complaints help services improve.

subject: CAR
body: Inclusion means
options: making sure everyone can take part and is valued
explanation: Diversity means recognising differences.

subject: CAR
body: If you see a colleague discriminating against someone, you should
options: challenge it if safe and report it to your manager
explanation: Discrimination is never acceptable.

subject: CAR
body: Which is an example of supporting independence?
options: doing everything for them to save time
encouraging a person to do as much as they can for themselves
explanation: Small choices matter.

subject: CAR
body: Barriers to communication can include
options: noise, poor lighting and a different first language
explanation: Adapt the environment and your approach.

subject: CAR
body: If a person uses a communication aid such as a picture board, you should
options: take it away to tidy up
use it with them and check understanding
ask their family to talk for them
explanation: Respect their preferred method.

subject: CAR
body: Personal information should be stored
explanation: Only share on a need-to-know basis.

subject: CAR
body: Calling people by the name they prefer is a way of
explanation: Ask how they would like to be addressed.

subject: CAR
body: Good hydration can help prevent
explanation: Encourage regular drinks.

subject: CAR
body: Before helping someone to eat, you should
options: start straight away while they're lying down
wash your hands and make sure they're sitting upright
feed them as quickly as possible
explanation: Go at their pace and keep them involved.

subject: CAR
topic: Standard 9: Mental health, dementia and learning disabilities
body: Dementia is
options: a normal part of ageing for everyone
a group of symptoms caused by diseases that damage the brain
explanation: Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause.

subject: CAR
topic: Standard 9: Mental health, dementia and learning disabilities
body: A learning disability
options: is the same as a mental illness
is lifelong and affects how a person learns and understands information
explanation: Support should be tailored to the person.

subject: CAR
body: Who should you report a safeguarding concern to first?
options: your manager or designated safeguarding lead, following policy
explanation: If someone is in immediate danger, call 999.

subject: CAR
body: Unexplained bruises in different stages of healing could be a sign of
explanation: Report and record what you see.

subject: CAR
body: If a child tells you they're being harmed, you should
options: promise to keep it a secret
ask them to write it down later
listen, not ask leading questions, and report it immediately
explanation: Follow your organisation's procedure.

subject: CAR
body: For an adult in cardiac arrest, chest compressions should be about
options: 5 to 6 cm deep at 100 to 120 per minute
1 to 2 cm deep at 60 per minute
explanation: Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest.

subject: CAR
body: For an adult who is choking and can't cough effectively, give
options: up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts
explanation: Call 999 if the obstruction doesn't clear.

subject: CAR
body: If you discover a fire, you should first
options: try to put it out alone
explanation: Then follow the fire procedure.

subject: CAR
body: Hazardous substances such as cleaning chemicals should be
options: stored securely in labelled containers as set out under COSHH
explanation: Mixing bleach with other products can give off toxic gas.

subject: CAR
body: Under the UK GDPR, personal information must be
options: kept secure, accurate and only for as long as needed
explanation: Breaches must be reported following policy.

subject: CAR
body: A good record should be
options: completed at the end of the week
explanation: Write it as soon as possible after the event.

subject: CAR
body: The chain of infection can be broken by
explanation: Breaking any link stops infection spreading.

subject: CAR
body: Hand washing with soap and water should take at least
options: 20 seconds of rubbing (about 40–60 seconds in total)
explanation: Cover all surfaces of the hands.

subject: CAR
body: Spillages of blood or body fluids should be
options: wiped with a dry tissue only
cleaned promptly using a spill kit and PPE
explanation: Follow your infection control policy.

subject: CAR
body: A reasonable adjustment for an autistic person could be
options: louder music in the waiting room
a quieter space and clear advance information
explanation: Ask the person what helps them.
